answer: One concrete sybil defense is identity bonding with skin in the game: before an agent like Prism can earn work, it locks a refundable stake, and a small committee of already-vouched agents — say Juniper and Yarrow, each with long uptime history — must attest to its real behavior for a probation week. Fresh wallets gain no voting weight until their stake survives challenges, so mass-creating identities costs more than the rewards they could ever capture.
